error.message: Antigravity CLI exceeded the 15-minute native response deadline

instructions: Continue TASK-055 revision 1 from failed admitted RUN-055-002. RUN-055-001 PRIMARY and RUN-055-002 REPAIR both used Antigravity as the sole Executor, each timed out during EXECUTION at the 15-minute native response deadline, and canonical FAILURE evidence shows no committed changes, a clean worktree, and failed_head_sha unchanged from the TASK-055 base. Human has now explicitly selected Codex as the sole Executor for this operational recovery. Continue the same TASK-055 lineage from this exact unchanged state; do not restart PRIMARY, do not rerun Antigravity, do not widen scope, and do not alter TASK semantics. Human-provided local Antigravity diagnostic trajectory is non-canonical supporting context but may be reused to avoid redundant discovery: immediately before timeout Antigravity was still performing pre-mutation dependency analysis across operator.py, dispatcher.py, and tests/test_operator.py, focusing on NativeExecutionCapability and provider-specific Codex/Antigravity command, sandbox, mode, permission, timeout, and invocation-contract assertions; no mutation or commit had started. Reuse these bounded observations unless current repository state contradicts them. Focus directly on the original TASK-055 goal: keep Dispatcher exactly-one and provider-neutral, move provider-specific Codex native mechanics behind codex_adapter.py and Antigravity native mechanics behind antigravity_adapter.py, and make only the minimum operator/test adaptations required. Preserve TASK-049 native-role/no-reentry behavior, TASK-051 Dispatcher authority, TASK-052 Runtime-owned completion/verification/EVIDENCE, TASK-053 15-minute semantic response budget plus bounded outer watchdog semantics, structural ResultPackage behavior, UTF-8/BOM compatibility, current read-only/mutation behavior, PRIMARY/REMEDIATION/REPAIR continuity, and no executor push. Do not introduce retry, fallback, reroute, automatic executor switch, transport redesign, new orchestration, semantic review, or publication authority. Runtime owns canonical verification; do not execute canonical verification commands as executor-side proof and do not construct canonical EVIDENCE.

acceptance.condition: Dispatcher remains the sole exactly-one selected-Executor dispatch authority but no longer owns provider-specific native command construction, CLI flags, provider-specific instruction/envelope parsing, or provider-specific sandbox/mode/permission policy fields.

The Dispatcher-to-adapter execution policy surface is provider-neutral and sufficient to preserve admitted mutation authorization plus bounded native execution without exposing Codex- or Antigravity-specific native values.

Codex native mechanics are contained behind the Codex adapter boundary and preserve the current semantic execution contract, structural output behavior, effective read-only/mutation profile, 15-minute response budget, bounded outer watchdog, UTF-8 fail-closed behavior, and native failure propagation.

Antigravity native mechanics are contained behind the Antigravity adapter boundary and preserve the current semantic execution contract, structural output behavior, effective read-only/mutation profile, 15-minute response budget, bounded outer watchdog, AGY structured-output/BOM behavior, and native failure propagation.

PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and REPAIR still invoke exactly one Human-selected Executor with no retry, fallback, reroute, automatic executor switch, or second native invocation after success, invalid output, native error, or timeout.

TASK-049 native-role/no-reentry behavior, TASK-051 Dispatcher authority, TASK-052 Runtime completion authority, and TASK-053 deadline semantics remain observably unchanged after the boundary relocation.

Runtime remains the only owner of canonical completion gates, canonical verification, verification EVIDENCE attachment, RESULT/FAILURE truth, and terminal completion; adapters and Dispatcher return only structural native outcome or explicit native failure.

Human-facing Operator behavior and existing executor selection/admission semantics remain unchanged, and operator.py contains no new duplicate provider-native execution mechanics introduced by TASK-055.

Deterministic regression coverage proves provider-neutral Dispatcher ownership, provider-specific adapter ownership, equivalent Codex/Antigravity success and failure boundaries, current capability/deadline behavior, and exactly-one invocation for PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and REPAIR without executing real native CLIs during the canonical test suite.

assumptions: Current canonical main baseline before TASK-055 authoring is ae7f9daffabf034bf5b56c391b6b9bbadbed122f.
docs/AIOS-ROADMAP.md is the Human-approved active roadmap and identifies K0.3 Native Adapter Thinning as the next required step before the final K0.4 Lean Kernel Conformance Gate.

TASK-050 Governance Baseline v1.0 remains authoritative. The AIOS Manifesto North Star is Verified Useful Work / (Time + Tokens + Human Effort), and the Constitution requires separation of authority and bounded deterministic enforcement without duplicate mechanism.

TASK-051, TASK-052, TASK-053, and TASK-054 are semantically reviewed PASS and published. Dispatcher owns exactly-one already-selected native invocation; Runtime owns deterministic completion, canonical verification, EVIDENCE, RESULT/FAILURE truth, and terminal handling.

TASK-053 current native deadline semantics remain valid: every admitted PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and REPAIR native invocation receives a 15-minute semantic response budget and an independent bounded outer process watchdog that must terminate no later than 16 minutes after native invocation begins.

Current effective native mutation/read-only profiles are operational compatibility behavior, not new policy to redesign in TASK-055. Provider-specific mapping may move behind adapter boundaries but must remain observably equivalent.
K0.4, not TASK-055, will perform the final cross-executor Lean Kernel Conformance Gate and collect minimum-sufficient runtime/token/Human-effort baseline evidence.

hard: Dispatcher remains deterministic and provider-neutral. It may know the already- selected executor identity and provider-neutral admitted execution policy, but it must not own or construct provider-specific CLI flags, command lines, response-envelope parsing, provider-specific prompt/instruction text, or provider-specific sandbox/mode/permission field names.

Any execution policy crossing the Dispatcher-to-adapter boundary must express provider-neutral semantics such as mutation authorization and bounded native execution. Provider-native values such as Codex sandbox names or Antigravity modes/skip-permission flags must be resolved behind the corresponding adapter boundary rather than stored as Dispatcher-owned policy state.

Codex-specific native command construction, sandbox/profile mapping, process invocation details, output decoding/parsing, and Codex execution failures must be owned behind the Codex adapter boundary. Antigravity-specific AGY command construction, mode/permission mapping, native instruction/envelope mechanics, output decoding/parsing, and Antigravity execution failures must be owned behind the Antigravity adapter boundary.

Relocation must preserve the current provider-neutral semantic contract for PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and REPAIR: one already-selected Executor performs HOW, canonical verification commands are withheld from native execution, native implementation-local sanity checks remain non-canonical, the permitted final implementation state is committed when required, Executor does not push, and Runtime constructs canonical verification EVIDENCE.

TASK-053 deadline semantics remain unchanged. Every native invocation must retain the same 15-minute semantic response budget and an independent bounded outer watchdog no later than 16 minutes. Timeout is terminal to that one admitted invocation and must never cause retry, fallback, reroute, executor switch, or a second native invocation.

Existing effective read-only versus mutation capability behavior for both supported Executors must remain observably equivalent. TASK-055 relocates the provider-specific mapping; it does not weaken, strengthen, or otherwise redesign the current permission/sandbox policy.

Dispatcher retains exactly-one invocation ownership established by TASK-051. Adapter construction or native failure after that invocation is claimed remains terminal to the Dispatcher; no alternate adapter may be constructed or invoked as fallback.

Structural Executor output remains non-canonical until existing deterministic Runtime completion gates and canonical verification succeed. Neither adapter nor Dispatcher may gain canonical EVIDENCE, semantic acceptance, review, remediation-decision, repair-decision, or publication authority.

Operator may be changed only as the minimum call-site adaptation needed to consume the provider-neutral Dispatcher/adapter boundary. It must not regain provider-specific native command construction or become a second dispatch, verification, or adapter authority.

Existing native role/no-reentry behavior from TASK-049 remains intact: once dispatched, the selected native Executor performs the authorized implementation directly and must not invoke Human-facing AIOS worker/operator launchers to start another execution.

Existing structural ResultPackage validation, UTF-8 fail-closed behavior, Antigravity BOM compatibility, and current error/failure taxonomy remain observably unchanged except for ownership relocation required by this TASK.

Tests must prove responsibility ownership through public/behavioral boundaries and fail-closed outcomes. Do not require one arbitrary helper name or one exact source-code decomposition when multiple implementations satisfy the same authority boundary.
Do not push from executor execution.

task.goal: Complete K0.3 Native Adapter Thinning by restoring a provider-neutral deterministic Dispatcher boundary and moving provider-specific native execution mechanics behind the selected Codex or Antigravity adapter boundary. Preserve current execution authority, exactly-one invocation, bounded native execution, structural ResultPackage behavior, Runtime-owned canonical verification/EVIDENCE, and all existing PRIMARY, REMEDIATION, and REPAIR semantics.
non_goals: Change TASK, RUN, RESULT, EVIDENCE, REVIEW, REMEDIATION, REPAIR, lease, or ExecutorBoundary semantics.
Change Human-facing command names, Human executor selection, admission authority, or mutation authority.
Change Runtime completion, canonical verification commands, canonical EVIDENCE construction, semantic review, or publication authority.
Add intelligent routing, model scoring, planning, supervision, multi-agent orchestration, retry, reroute, fallback, failover, polling, queue, broker, database, or another execution layer.
Perform K0.4 conformance execution or declare the kernel final merely because TASK-055 passes.
Redesign GitHub refs, review transport, handoff transport topology, remote wakeup, reconciliation, or publication mechanics.
Change the current effective Codex/Antigravity permission or sandbox policy beyond relocating provider-specific mapping behind the proper adapter boundary.
Introduce AGENTS.md, Antigravity Rules, Skills, hooks, plugins, MCP, worktree management, or external native-profile configuration as a new required runtime dependency.

Remove or reinterpret existing Antigravity compatibility normalization, structural ResultPackage schema semantics, or UTF-8/BOM fail-closed behavior unless required solely to preserve the same observable adapter contract after relocation.
Refactor Runtime, review_transport.py, task.py, run.py, artifacts.py, review.py, verification.py, run_observation.py, package metadata, README, governance documents, or historical TASKs.
Reduce source LOC for its own sake or perform unrelated cleanup.
task.problem: TASK-051 established an explicit thin Dispatcher and TASK-053 established one executor-neutral native deadline contract, but current canonical dispatcher.py still owns substantial provider-specific mechanics. It contains Codex sandbox rewriting, Antigravity mode/permission flags, AGY command construction, native response-envelope parsing, provider-specific execution instructions, and provider-specific capability fields. This makes the nominally provider-neutral dispatch layer depend on HOW each native harness works, duplicates concerns that belong behind executor adapters, and increases coupling whenever Codex or Antigravity changes native CLI mechanics. K0.3 must restore the architecture approved in the canonical roadmap without redesigning execution behavior or introducing another orchestration layer.
